chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Peanuts: great trumpet, no tone, and his death
summary: Peanuts played powerfully but never had a good tone; he died after saying he could not understand why he lived without playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: SO THIS IS WHERE P. CAME IN.
P. was in the band then and Stuff.
HE NEVER HAD A GOOD TONE.
He never had a good tone.
BUT HE NEVER HAD A GOOD TONE.

No, I know that on "After You've Gone." I wonder why he was kind of powerful in the background he wanted to take that place, if it was left up to the rest of us, he would have had it written out probably.
Yeah, we couldn't have him taking the lead on the first chorus. But he played a hell of a trumpet in that thing. HE WAS A VERY ADVANCED GUY FOR THAT TIME.
They did look up to him. He was a little short guy. He was always sensitive about being short. He wore real high heel shoes, he looked as if he was going to tip over.
He died not so many months ago after I saw him. He was a little disgusted, he said that I don't know why God let's me stay on this earth and I can't play my horn.
I know, but he was still disgusted. He had something in the back of his head.
I don't know what it was. One of the doctors told him that if he played anymore, it would kill him.
